subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — context window & token limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finco.com>, Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro.ruiz@finco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up — context window & token limits

Hi Jane / Alejandro,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the FinCo use case. This follow-up captures the items we discussed and the clarifying questions we need to validate performance expectations before the POC.

Quick recap of what you shared:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + risk highlight extraction from multi-turn chat history.
- Typical request size: 6–10 previous messages + new user message (avg 1.2k input tokens).
- Desired output: short summary + 3 risk flags (avg 200–400 output tokens).
- Target latency: 95th percentile < 800ms for single-request interactive flows; background batch/rerank can be higher.
- Expected concurrency: 60 concurrent interactive users at peak; burst to 120 for spikes.
- Streaming requirement: prefer token-by-token streaming for UI responsiveness on the agent desktop.

Clarifying questions we need to lock the SLOs and test plan:
1) Confirm max context window we should assume for the POC (you mentioned up to ~8k tokens worst-case including system prompt — is that the absolute worst-case we should test?).
2) Is the 1.2k input you quoted inclusive of any metadata/system prompts or should we treat system prompt as additional tokens?
3) For streaming: do you require initial chunk latency < 200ms to start streaming, or is startup < 500ms acceptable provided token cadence is steady?
4) Can you share a small set (3–5) representative message examples (redacted) so we can run local perf sims with realistic token lengths?

Next steps from our side:
- Dev will produce a perf-run worksheet and baseline scripts to simulate your request size distribution and concurrency.
- We'll propose a POC plan with 1) latency-only test (single-shot), 2) streaming startup + throughput, 3) concurrency soak.
- Draft an SLA language for latency targets and fallbacks (sending attached SLA draft).

Attaching: redwood-performance-run-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet for you to validate workloads) and an SLA draft that maps proposed SLOs to service behavior.

Can you reply with the answers to 1–3 above and share 3 redacted examples when you have a moment? If it's easier, we can hop on a 20-min follow-up to lock assumptions.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — context window & token limits

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary. Quick answers below:

1) Context window: 8k tokens is our realistic upper bound today (includes all conversation history but excludes downstream metadata). For POC please test 8k and also a mid-case at 4k.
2) The 1.2k input is user+conversation content only. We add a small system prompt (~60 tokens) and an LLM metadata wrapper (~30 tokens) on top — you can treat those as additive. So worst-case request ~1.3–1.4k tokens typical, 8k for long histories.
3) Streaming: ideal is initial token to UI < 250ms. If that isn't achievable at first, we can accept < 500ms as a phased approach, but 250ms is the goal for agent experience.

Examples: attached two redacted chat transcripts as PDFs — they illustrate the 1.2k typical and a longer 7.3k-case. Note: a few transcripts also include embedded JSON blobs we strip for PII.

Other notes:
- Concurrency: 60 steady concurrent interactive sessions is accurate; we may see short spikes to 150 but those should be handled via queuing/fallback (we can negotiate burst behavior in the SLA).
- For the POC, we care most about 95th pct latency and streaming start time; 99th pct is nice-to-know.

I'll loop procurement when we reach SLA language. Alejandro — can you confirm if procurement needs any additional docs for security/evidence before we sign a POC SOW?

Best,
Jane

Thanks Jane — that's perfect and helpful. Next steps:

1) Dev will run two perf sims for the POC:
   - Typical path: 1.3k request + ~300 token response (steady-state, 60 concurrency)
   - Stress path: 8k request + 400 token response (spike tests, scale to 150 burst)

2) We'll instrument streaming startup time and report 50/95/99 pct start latencies and token cadence (tokens/sec) to validate UX constraints. We'll also export CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates.

3) I'll send a proposed POC timeline and runbook by EOD (attaching the performance worksheet and an updated SLA draft for review).

4) For procurement: if you can share a standard NDA/POC SOW template, we can pair legal and procurement to speed this.

Proposed quick sync: Wed 4/7 10:00–10:20 PT to review the worksheet and agree on the POC run dates — does that work for Alejandro / Jane?

If so, I'll calendar and add Dev + Rishi to the invite.

Marissa
